Linear regression is both a statistical model and one of the simplest supervised-learning algorithms.

That makes it an ideal bridge between statistics and machine learning.

::: {.callout-tip}
## What you will learn
- The linear model and least squares
- Residuals and the loss surface
- Coefficient interpretation
- Diagnostics and assumptions
- How regression connects to regularized ML
:::

## The model

For one predictor,

$$
Y=\beta_0+\beta_1X+\varepsilon.
$$

Least squares chooses coefficients minimizing

$$
SSE(\beta_0,\beta_1)
=
\sum_{i=1}^n
\left(y_i-\beta_0-\beta_1x_i\right)^2.
$$

## Interactive: fit the line yourself

```{ojs}
//| echo: false
viewof b0 = Inputs.range([-3,3], {value:0, step:.1, label:"Intercept β₀"})
viewof b1 = Inputs.range([-1,4], {value:1, step:.1, label:"Slope β₁"})
rlr=d3.randomLcg(.19)
ptslr=d3.range(45).map(i=>{let x=i/7; return{x,y:1+2*x+(rlr()-.5)*3}})
sselr=d3.sum(ptslr,d=>(d.y-(b0+b1*d.x))**2)
html`<div class="ms-readout"><span>Sum of squared errors</span><b>${sselr.toFixed(1)}</b></div>`
```

```{ojs}
//| echo: false
lineLR=[{x:0,y:b0},{x:6.5,y:b0+b1*6.5}]
Plot.plot({
 height:340,x:{label:"x"},y:{label:"y"},
 marks:[Plot.dot(ptslr,{x:"x",y:"y",fill:"#4F46E5"}),Plot.line(lineLR,{x:"x",y:"y",stroke:"#E11D48",strokeWidth:3})]
})
```

Try to minimize SSE manually. Optimization algorithms do the same search much faster.

## Residuals tell the story

A residual is

$$
e_i=y_i-\hat y_i.
$$

Residual plots can reveal:

```text
curve pattern     → missing nonlinearity
funnel shape      → nonconstant variance
clusters          → missing groups/features
large residuals   → unusual cases
```

## 3D loss surface

```{python}
#| code-fold: true
import numpy as np
import plotly.graph_objects as go

rng=np.random.default_rng(9)
x=np.linspace(0,5,50); y=1+2*x+rng.normal(0,1,50)
B0=np.linspace(-1,3,70); B1=np.linspace(.5,3.5,70)
Z=np.array([[np.sum((y-(a+b*x))**2) for b in B1] for a in B0])
fig=go.Figure(go.Surface(x=B1,y=B0,z=Z,showscale=False))
fig.update_layout(height=430,scene=dict(xaxis_title="β1",yaxis_title="β0",zaxis_title="SSE"))
fig.show()
```

The bowl is the optimization landscape for this simple model.

## DS/ML Bridge: regularization

Multiple linear regression:

$$
\hat y=\beta_0+\sum_{j=1}^p\beta_jx_j.
$$

Ridge adds an $L_2$ penalty:

$$
\text{Loss}
=
SSE+\lambda\sum_j\beta_j^2.
$$

Lasso uses an $L_1$ penalty:

$$
\text{Loss}
=
SSE+\lambda\sum_j|\beta_j|.
$$

Now the statistical model connects directly to ML ideas of generalization, regularization and bias–variance trade-offs.

## Summary
- Linear regression minimizes squared residuals.
- Coefficients describe conditional linear relationships.
- Residual diagnostics reveal model misspecification.
- Regression can be used for inference, prediction, or both—but the goal changes how it should be evaluated.
- Ridge and lasso extend regression into regularized machine learning.
